wayland.step1: Open <gnome>Settings → Keyboard → Custom Shortcuts</gnome> (GNOME) or <kde>System Settings → Shortcuts → Custom Shortcuts</kde> (KDE).

setup.introMac: Vicu reads the URL from the active browser tab using AppleScript when Quick Entry opens. This works with Chrome, Safari, Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi, and Arc. Firefox has limited support. Browser extensions provide instant (<1ms) detection; without them Vicu falls back to AppleScript (~300ms).
setup.introOther: Vicu automatically reads the URL bar from the active browser window when Quick Entry opens. This works with Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Brave, Opera, and Vivaldi. Browser extensions provide instant (<1ms) detection; without them Vicu falls back to Windows accessibility APIs (~300ms).
setup.macNoSetup: No setup needed for Chrome, Safari, Edge, Brave, Vivaldi, and Arc. On first use, macOS will ask you to allow Vicu to control the browser.
setup.hint: Open Quick Entry while a browser tab is active to see the link hint.

firefox.title: Firefox (extension for instant detection)
firefox.macWarning: Firefox fallback detection via AppleScript is unreliable on macOS. Installing the extension is strongly recommended for Firefox support.
firefox.step1: Open the extensions/browser folder and locate the .xpi file
firefox.step3: Click the gear icon → “Install Add-on From File…”

chrome.title: Chrome (optional extension for instant detection)
chrome.intro: Chrome works without the extension, but installing it provides instant (<1ms) detection instead of the ~300ms fallback.
chrome.step4: Copy the Extension ID shown on the card and paste it in the field above

others.titleMac: Safari, Arc, Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi
others.autoMac: No setup needed. Vicu detects URLs automatically via AppleScript.
others.autoOther: No setup needed. Vicu detects URLs automatically via accessibility APIs.

rest.title: <name>1. Local REST API</name> (by Adam Coddington)
rest.step1: Open Obsidian → Settings (gear icon, bottom-left) → Community Plugins → Browse
rest.step3: Go back to Settings → scroll to “Local REST API” under Community Plugins
rest.step4: The API Key is shown at the top of the plugin's settings panel — click the copy button and paste it below
rest.step5: Leave all other settings at their defaults (HTTPS on port 27124)

uri.title: <name>2. Advanced URI</name> (by Vinzent03)
uri.step1: Same steps — search “Advanced URI” in Community Plugins → Install → Enable
uri.step2: In the plugin settings, turn on “Use UID instead of file paths”
uri.step3: This makes note links survive file renames. All other settings can stay at their defaults.
uri.step4: Vicu adds a <prop>uid</prop> property to a note only when you save a task linked to it; notes you do not link are never changed.

setup.done: Once both plugins are enabled and Obsidian is running, click Test Connection below to verify.

secretNotice.keyObfuscatedBodyLinux: On Linux, Vicu does not use the system keyring. Your provider key is saved in a file in Vicu's data folder that is only obscured, not protected by a key. Anyone who can read your user profile can recover it. Only the file's permissions protect it.
secretNotice.tokenObfuscatedBodyLinux: On Linux, Vicu does not use the system keyring. Your sign-in token is saved in a file in Vicu's data folder that is only obscured, not protected by a key. Anyone who can read your user profile can recover it. Only the file's permissions protect it.

voice.title: Voice input
voice.intro: Hold the + button and say a task such as “Call mom tomorrow 3pm”. Let go to add it, press Esc to cancel. It goes where the list you are looking at puts new tasks, unless you name a project or date. With a shortcut set below, hold it the same way, or tap it to keep listening until you press it again or Enter. “Say a task” in the command palette works without holding anything.
voice.smart: With smart dictation on (Settings, Assistant), tapping the shortcut or sliding up from a held + starts smart dictation instead: keep talking and the tasks appear as cards.

assistant.cleartext: This address is not encrypted (http) and is outside your local network: your key and what you send can be read on the way. Use https.

thinking.title: Thinking
thinking.intro: The model that turns your words into tasks and answers your questions. It runs at your provider.
thinking.requests: Requests go straight from this computer to the provider you choose, with your key; Vicu has no server in between and shows no prices.
thinking.keyPlaceholderSaved: A key is saved. Paste a new one to replace it.
thinking.keyNote: Kept in this computer’s secret store, like your Vikunja sign-in. It is never synced or shown again.

features.title: Features
features.intro: Holding + (or the voice shortcut) and letting go always adds one task at once, without the model.
features.dictationHow: Tap the voice shortcut, or hold + and slide up to the sparkle, then keep talking: tasks appear as cards while you talk. Also Break into steps (right-click a task) and Make tasks from text (command palette).
features.brainDumpHow: Slide up from a held + or tap the voice shortcut, then turn on Brain dump in the sheet (or choose Brain dump in the command palette). Talk or type as long as you like; Organize sorts it all into projects, subprojects, tasks, subtasks and notes for you to check.
features.askHow: Press the Ask button next to Search, or {{keys}}. Changes are proposed on cards you apply.
features.talkHow: Turn on the microphone in Ask and just talk; answers are read aloud and it keeps listening.
features.notesHow: Typed notes, PDFs and photos of pages, from the command palette or by dropping files on Vicu. Pictures need a model that reads them.

result.canRunNone: This model can run none of the features.

consent.title: Send data to {{provider}}?
consent.intro: The assistant sends this to {{provider}} with your key, and only when you use it:
consent.dictation: Dictation: the text of what you said or pasted (never audio), your project, label and place names, the list you are in, and the date, time and time zone.
consent.ask: Ask and Talk: your messages, an overview (counts, project, label and custom list names), and the tasks it looks up, including the names of people in shared projects.
consent.neverSent: Never sent: audio (speech is recognised on this computer), hidden tasks, comment texts, attachments, your Vikunja token, your server address, place positions.
consent.notes: Notes: the text of the notes you add, their title and date, and the same names as dictation plus people you share projects with. Pictures of pages only after you agree to that separately.

speech.title: Hearing
speech.intro: Turns your voice into text on this computer; audio never leaves it. Without a downloaded model, the system’s speech recognition is used.
speech.introLinux: Turns your voice into text on this computer; audio never leaves it. Without a downloaded model, the system’s speech recognition is used (Linux has none).
speech.usedBy: Used by every voice feature: quick capture, smart dictation and Talk. Only the text goes to the model under Thinking.
speech.notInBuild: Local speech is not part of this build of Vicu.
speech.parakeet: Parakeet models detect the language themselves.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.text: Conversations (the last five) and transcripts kept after a failed request stay on this computer and are deleted when you sign out. The assistant’s settings and key stay with this computer.
